claims.title: Forward loss-clock compiler for coupled passive Gaussian memory

quoted_fields.interface: The frozen second-stage return proposes a constructive forward contraction/loss-clock consumer for classically described coupled passive Gaussian memory with noncommuting system interactions, rank-deficient loss and dark modes. It earns explicit source/clock/count/cutoff and finite-arithmetic arguments for logarithmic passive-stiffness dependence, while whole-proof review, practical crossover and physical performance remain unestablished.
quoted_fields.failure: New author-derived whole conjunction, not independently whole-proof reviewed, gate/hardware executed, historically established or practically superior. Known finite classical passive H/E, retained vacuum, actual precision-capable controlled system block encodings and paid normalizations/access are inputs. Arbitrary reference and prescribed instrument records are outputs; bath/physical loss records remain private. Finite arithmetic, clock/cutoff/count/amplification costs and large horizon overhead remain. Strong ordinary slow-memory reduction defeats treating the stiffness sweep as a runtime advantage. Existing first-stage status and N1510 actual accepted independent-mode/algebra scopes remain, without acceptance transfer to this new source. No Capital reproof/replay/novelty/sign-off or researcher contact.
